Blocks.Text: Talent CRM Connect integration partners will naturally encounter errors as a result of data validation errors, transient infrastructure issues, or other causes. How partners empower their customers to resolve their own issues or seek help can reduce the operational load placed on engineering and support teams in our respective organizations.
This guide makes recommendations for a minimum set of error handling and logging capabilities in order to empower users to self-serve and effectively seek assistance.
Customers occasionally will need to re-enable CRM Connect. Re-enabling CRM Connect consists of:

removing existing integration values stored in the CRM like urn:li:organization:{id}, etc.
re-enabling CRM Connect through the onboarding plugin as described in the customer configuration documentation.
Partners should be able to support this flow through managed process that support teams or even customers can perform.
Data sent to LinkedIn will be persisted unless deleted. If a customer re-enables within a CRM, it is up to CRM partners to determine if data should be deleted from previous enablements.

API requests failures frequently need detailed error logging to determine the root cause. In order to accelerate support issue resolution and empower customers to ask for help, it is recommended that partners store detailed error logs and make them available to customers in the event of API request failures.

When errors are encountered, logs should record details of the failure. Some request formats, like BATCH_UPDATE and BATCH_GET request methods, return 200 HTTP status codes even if some of the request elements fail. Partners should treat these requests as failures in their logging for the purposes of future troubleshooting. Error logs should record:

the full request, including URL, request headers, and request body
response headers and body, and status code. It is especially important to log the x-li-uuid response header
Details of request failures can be made available to customers, but access tokens in the request headers should be masked or removed.

Partner support teams and customers should have access to detailed error logs to simplify support requests and load on engineering teams. Partners are strongly encouraged to make access to detailed errors a component of end user workflow to resolve issues like data validation problems encountered when syncing data between the CRM and LinkedIn.
Retry when there may be an intermittent issue with LinkedIn infrastructure. Whether to retry depends on the response:

Rows.Text: For BATCH requests, check for failed elements. Retry only those elements.
Retry the request. If it fails again, do not retry.
Request a new access token, then retry.
Retry the request. If it fails again, do not retry.
Rate limit reached. Retry after midnight UTC.
Retry the request. If it fails again, do not retry.
Retry the request. If it fails again, do not retry.
Retry the request. If it fails again, do not retry.

Blocks.Text: Partners may adapt this retry strategy to their needs, as long as the behavior is clear and LinkedIn's guidance is respected.

The following examples show typical error responses for Talent CRM Connect (and related) APIs. Always capture and store the x-li-uuid response header when an error occurs; provide it when reporting the issue to LinkedIn support.
Important response header to save on errors:
x-li-uuid: AAZLFYFBm9/EcmxFuiti+Q==
Provide this value when contacting the LinkedIn team about the failure.

Response: 500 Internal Server Error

Action: Retry the request. If the error persists, report it to LinkedIn support and include the full response and the x-li-uuid header.

Log full request and response (including x-li-uuid) for every error.
For 200 responses with batch methods, treat any non-empty errors as a failure and log it.
Mask or remove tokens before sharing logs.
Use the retry table above to decide when to retry.
When contacting LinkedIn about an error, always provide the x-li-uuid value from the error response.
